entities.summary: Aphytis, also Aphyte (Ἀφύτη) and Aphytus or Aphytos (Ἄφυτος), was an ancient Greek city in Pallene, the westernmost headland of Chalcidice. Around the middle of the 8th century BC colonists from Euboea arrived. The city became well known for its Temple of Dionysus, which appears to have been built in the second half of the 8th century BC. At Aphytis, Ammon was worshipped, at least from the time of the Spartan general Lysander, as zealously as in Ammonium, sanctuary in Libya. According to Pausanias, the patron of Aphytis, Ammon Zeus, appeared in a dream to Lysander and urged him to raise the siege, which he did.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Aphytis was a significant regional center in ancient Greece, known for its Temple of Dionysus and its role as a sanctuary for Ammon worship. Its patronage by Lysander led to the appearance of Ammon Zeus in a dream, which influenced his decision to raise the siege.
